title: Sport & Society
subtitle: Debate the money, ethics, and legacy behind modern sport

lessons.title: Le sport professionnel
lessons.description: Examine how professional sport really makes its money — transfers, TV rights, and salaries.

blocks.heading: L'économie d'un club professionnel
blocks.body: A professional club rarely lives on ticket sales alone. Modern revenue rests on three pillars: la billetterie (match-day tickets and season passes), les droits télévisés (fees broadcasters pay to air matches), and le sponsoring (brands paying to be associated with the club's image). When one pillar wobbles — an empty stadium, a lost TV deal — the whole budget feels it.

examples.french: La billetterie ne représente plus qu'une petite part des recettes du club.
examples.english: Ticketing now represents only a small share of the club's revenue.

examples.french: Les droits télévisés se négocient plusieurs années à l'avance.
examples.english: TV rights are negotiated several years in advance.

examples.french: Sans sponsoring, beaucoup de clubs seraient déficitaires.
examples.english: Without sponsorship, many clubs would be running a deficit.

examples.french: Le budget du club dépend surtout de sa visibilité télévisée.
examples.english: The club's budget depends mainly on its TV visibility.

examples.french: Une chaîne payante a acquis l'exclusivité du championnat.
examples.english: A pay channel acquired exclusive rights to the championship.

blocks.tip: "Les droits télévisés" is always plural in French — never say "le droit télévisé" for this meaning.

blocks.heading: Le marché des transferts
blocks.body: Clubs buy and sell players like a company trades assets. A transfer moves a player from one club to another, usually against une indemnité de transfert (a transfer fee) paid to the selling club. A clause libératoire fixes in advance the price at which a player can leave — it protects the player but can also fuel une surenchère (a bidding war) between rich clubs.

examples.french: L'attaquant a signé un contrat de quatre ans après son transfert.
examples.english: The forward signed a four-year contract after his transfer.

examples.french: Sa clause libératoire s'élève à quarante millions d'euros.
examples.english: His release clause stands at forty million euros.

examples.english: Two clubs engaged in a real bidding war for the player.

examples.french: La valeur marchande d'un joueur peut chuter après une blessure.
examples.english: A player's market value can drop after an injury.

blocks.tip: "Le mercato" (borrowed from Italian) is the everyday French word for the transfer window.

blocks.heading: Le grand écart des salaires
blocks.body: The gap between a star player's salary and an average worker's pay fuels a recurring debate. Defenders point to short careers and rare talent; critics call some salaries mirobolants (astronomical) and out of proportion. To limit this, competitions can impose le fair-play financier — rules requiring clubs to spend roughly within their means rather than relying on a wealthy owner's money indefinitely.

examples.french: Certains dénoncent des salaires mirobolants dans le football professionnel.
examples.english: Some people denounce astronomical salaries in professional football.

examples.french: Le fair-play financier oblige les clubs à équilibrer leurs comptes.

blocks.heading: La voix passive dans le compte rendu économique
blocks.body: Sports journalism leans heavily on the passive voice to foreground the fact, not the actor: "le joueur a été transféré" rather than "le club a transféré le joueur." Form it with être + past participle, agreeing with the subject. The agent, when mentioned, follows "par." This register feels formal and neutral — ideal for reporting figures and decisions without taking sides.

examples.french: Le contrat a été signé hier soir par les deux parties.
examples.english: The contract was signed last night by both parties.

examples.french: Les droits télévisés sont vendus par lots de trois ans.
examples.english: TV rights are sold in three-year packages.

examples.english: The budget is revised every summer by the board.

blocks.tip: When the agent is obvious or unimportant, French often drops "par..." entirely: "Le joueur a été transféré" is complete on its own.

blocks.heading: Comparer les chiffres : comparatif et superlatif
blocks.body: Debating sport's economics means constantly comparing figures. Use plus/moins/aussi + adjective + que for comparisons, and le/la plus / le/la moins for superlatives. Watch the irregulars: bon → meilleur (not "plus bon"), and remember que introduces the second term of comparison.

blocks.tip: "Meilleur" is the irregular comparative of "bon" — but "plus mauvais" and "pire" can both work for "worse," with "pire" sounding more emphatic.

passages.title: L'AS Vallenoire, un club sous tension financière
passages.french:
L'AS Vallenoire a longtemps été un club discret, connu pour son centre de formation plutôt que pour ses folies financières.
Cette saison, tout a changé : le club a battu son record de transfert en recrutant l'attaquant Karim Lassalle pour vingt-huit millions d'euros.
Cette somme, versée en trois fois, a été en partie financée par un nouvel actionnaire, un fonds d'investissement basé à l'étranger.
Selon la direction, ce transfert devait relancer une équipe jugée trop prévisible et redonner de la visibilité au sponsor principal.
Mais les comptes racontent une autre histoire : malgré des droits télévisés en hausse, le club affiche un déficit de neuf millions d'euros.
Les dépenses, elles, ont explosé : le salaire de Lassalle serait, d'après plusieurs journaux sportifs, le plus élevé de l'histoire du club.
Certains supporters dénoncent un salaire mirobolant et craignent que le fair-play financier ne rattrape bientôt l'AS Vallenoire.
D'autres estiment au contraire que l'investissement est nécessaire pour rester compétitif face à des clubs mieux dotés.
Le propriétaire, de son côté, assure que le club sera rentable dès l'an prochain, une fois la nouvelle billetterie mise en place.
Un nouvel abonnement, plus abordable pour les familles, doit d'ailleurs être lancé à la rentrée.
Reste à savoir si la valeur marchande de Lassalle justifiera, à terme, une indemnité de transfert aussi élevée.
Pour l'instant, le pari reste risqué, et le club joue gros, sur le terrain comme dans ses comptes.
passages.english:
AS Vallenoire was long a low-key club, known for its training academy rather than financial extravagance.
This season, everything changed: the club broke its transfer record by signing forward Karim Lassalle for twenty-eight million euros.
This sum, paid in three instalments, was partly financed by a new shareholder, a foreign-based investment fund.
According to management, this transfer was meant to revive a team seen as too predictable and boost visibility for the main sponsor.
But the accounts tell another story: despite rising TV rights, the club shows a nine-million-euro deficit.
Expenses, meanwhile, have exploded: Lassalle's salary is, according to several sports newspapers, the highest in the club's history.
Some supporters denounce an astronomical salary and fear that financial fair play will soon catch up with AS Vallenoire.
Others argue that the investment is necessary to stay competitive against better-funded clubs.
The owner, for his part, insists the club will be profitable next year, once the new ticketing system is in place.
A new season pass, more affordable for families, is also set to launch in the autumn.
It remains to be seen whether Lassalle's market value will eventually justify such a high transfer fee.
For now, the gamble remains risky, and the club has a lot riding on it, both on the pitch and in its accounts.

lessons.title: Dopage et éthique
lessons.description: Discuss doping allegations, testing, and sanctions with careful, attributed language.

blocks.heading: Qu'est-ce que le dopage ?
blocks.body: Le dopage means using a produit dopant (banned substance) or method to artificially boost athletic performance. To catch it, federations run un contrôle antidopage: an échantillon (sample) of blood or urine is analysed, and the result is either negative or positive. A positive result triggers an investigation before any sanction — the process is meant to be rigorous precisely because an athlete's reputation is at stake.

examples.french: L'athlète a été soumis à un contrôle antidopage après la course.
examples.english: The athlete underwent a doping test after the race.

examples.french: Le produit dopant retrouvé dans l'échantillon reste à confirmer.
examples.english: The banned substance found in the sample still needs to be confirmed.

examples.french: Un test positif ne signifie pas automatiquement une sanction immédiate.
examples.english: A positive test doesn't automatically mean an immediate sanction.

examples.french: L'agence antidopage a renforcé ses contrôles cette saison.
examples.english: The anti-doping agency stepped up its testing this season.

examples.french: Le règlement de la fédération prévoit une contre-expertise en cas de doute.
examples.english: The federation's rules provide for a second analysis in case of doubt.

blocks.tip: "Dopage" is uncountable in French — say "le dopage" or "des cas de dopage," never "un dopage."

blocks.heading: Accusations et présomption d'innocence
blocks.body: When an accusation surfaces, careful language matters: a suspicion (un soupçon) is not proof (une preuve), and an athlete remains presumed innocent — la présomption d'innocence — until the enquête (investigation) concludes. Journalists often use the conditional to report an unconfirmed claim: "le coureur aurait pris un produit interdit" signals that this is alleged, not established.

examples.french: Selon l'agence, le coureur aurait pris un produit interdit avant la course.
examples.english: According to the agency, the cyclist reportedly took a banned product before the race.

examples.french: L'athlète nie fermement toute accusation de dopage.
examples.english: The athlete firmly denies any doping accusation.

examples.french: Rien ne prouve encore sa culpabilité : l'enquête est en cours.
examples.english: Nothing yet proves her guilt: the investigation is ongoing.

examples.french: Un simple soupçon ne suffit pas à justifier une sanction.
examples.english: A mere suspicion is not enough to justify a sanction.

examples.french: Son entraîneur a démenti les rumeurs dès leur apparition.
examples.english: Her coach denied the rumours as soon as they appeared.

blocks.tip: Attribute contested claims explicitly: "selon...", "d'après...", or the conditional tense keep your French both accurate and fair.

blocks.heading: Les conséquences d'un scandale
blocks.body: A confirmed case brings une sanction: often une suspension (a ban from competition), sometimes une disqualification of past results, and in serious repeat cases une sanction à vie. Beyond the rules, there's the human cost: une image ternie (a tarnished image) and, for some, a slow réhabilitation once they publicly reconnaissent les faits (acknowledge the facts) rather than continuing to nier.

examples.french: La fédération a prononcé une suspension de deux ans.
examples.english: The federation handed down a two-year suspension.

examples.french: Ses résultats ont été annulés après sa disqualification.
examples.english: Her results were cancelled following her disqualification.

examples.french: Il a fini par reconnaître les faits, des années après le scandale.
examples.english: He eventually acknowledged the facts, years after the scandal.

examples.french: Sa réhabilitation a pris du temps, mais le public lui a pardonné.
examples.english: His rehabilitation took time, but the public forgave him.

examples.french: L'exemplarité est essentielle pour restaurer la confiance du public.
examples.english: Exemplary conduct is essential to restore public trust.

blocks.tip: "Nier" (to deny) and "dénoncer" (to expose/report) look similar but mean opposite things — don't mix them up in a debate.

blocks.heading: Le conditionnel pour l'information non confirmée
blocks.body: French journalism uses the conditional tense specifically to signal an unverified claim — a crucial tool when reporting an accusation fairly. "Le coureur aurait pris un produit interdit" means "the cyclist allegedly took a banned product" — not a stated fact. Compare with the indicative "a pris," which would assert it as certain. This distinction protects both the accused and the accuracy of the reporting.

examples.french: Selon des sources proches du dossier, l'athlète serait dans le collimateur de l'agence.

examples.english: The investigation, it's said, is reportedly about to conclude.

blocks.tip: Always pair the conditional with a source ("selon...", "d'après...", "dit-on") — the tense alone signals doubt, but naming the source keeps your writing credible.

blocks.heading: Le subjonctif après le doute et l'opinion
blocks.body: Verbs and expressions of doubt, possibility, or subjective judgement trigger the subjunctive: il est possible que, il se peut que, je doute que, bien qu'il affirme que (even though he claims that). This lets you weigh both sides of a doping case without asserting either as fact — essential for balanced, B2-level argumentation.

examples.english: Although she denied the facts, the evidence piled up.

blocks.tip: "Bien que" and "quoique" both mean "although" and both require the subjunctive — but "quoique" feels slightly more formal.

passages.title: Une accusation qui divise
passages.french:
À une semaine des Championnats d'Estivale, la sprinteuse Élodie Brancart se retrouve au cœur d'une polémique.
Selon l'Agence de Vigilance Sportive, un échantillon prélevé lors d'une compétition précédente contiendrait des traces d'un produit dopant.
Le résultat, encore provisoire, doit être confirmé par une contre-expertise avant toute décision officielle.
Dans un communiqué, Brancart affirme son innocence et dénonce une fuite qui, selon elle, viole le règlement sur la confidentialité.
"Je n'ai jamais pris de produit interdit et je fais confiance à la procédure", a-t-elle déclaré.
Son entraîneur va plus loin : il évoque une possible erreur de laboratoire et réclame une nouvelle analyse indépendante.
L'Agence, de son côté, rappelle que la présomption d'innocence s'applique tant que l'enquête n'est pas close.
Certains observateurs jugent la fuite injuste envers l'athlète, avant même toute conclusion officielle.
D'autres estiment au contraire que la transparence sert l'intégrité du sport, même lorsqu'elle est inconfortable.
La fédération a annoncé qu'aucune sanction ne serait prononcée avant la fin de la contre-expertise.
Si le second test confirmait le premier, une suspension serait probable ; s'il l'infirmait, Brancart courrait librement dès le mois prochain.
En attendant, l'athlète continue de s'entraîner, sous le regard attentif de la presse sportive.
passages.english:
One week before the Estivale Championships, sprinter Élodie Brancart finds herself at the centre of a controversy.
According to the Sports Vigilance Agency, a sample taken during a previous competition reportedly contains traces of a banned substance.
The result, still provisional, must be confirmed by a second analysis before any official decision.
In a statement, Brancart maintains her innocence and denounces a leak that, she says, violates confidentiality rules.
"I have never taken a banned substance and I trust the process," she declared.
Her coach goes further: he suggests a possible lab error and is calling for a new, independent analysis.
The Agency, for its part, points out that the presumption of innocence applies as long as the investigation remains open.
Some observers consider the leak unfair to the athlete, even before any official conclusion.
Others argue that transparency serves the integrity of the sport, even when it is uncomfortable.
The federation announced that no sanction would be handed down before the second analysis is complete.
If the second test confirmed the first, a suspension would be likely; if it disproved it, Brancart would race freely as of next month.
In the meantime, the athlete continues training, under the watchful eye of the sports press.

lessons.title: Les grands événements
lessons.description: Weigh the costs and benefits of hosting major sporting events, from stadiums to legacy.

blocks.heading: Organiser un grand événement
blocks.body: Hosting a major sporting event starts years earlier, with une candidature (a bid) submitted by a ville hôte. If chosen, a comité d'organisation coordinates everything: building infrastructure, stadiums, and le village des athlètes. All of this is planned against un budget prévisionnel — a forecast that, in practice, is frequently exceeded, producing un dépassement de coûts that taxpayers ultimately absorb.

examples.french: La ville a déposé sa candidature pour accueillir les Jeux d'Aurenne.
examples.english: The city submitted its bid to host the Aurenne Games.

examples.french: Le comité d'organisation doit livrer les infrastructures dans les délais.
examples.english: The organising committee must deliver the infrastructure on schedule.

examples.french: Le budget prévisionnel a été largement dépassé.
examples.english: The forecast budget was significantly exceeded.

examples.french: Le village des athlètes accueillera plus de dix mille sportifs.
examples.english: The athletes' village will host more than ten thousand competitors.

examples.french: Un dépassement de coûts pareil inquiète les contribuables locaux.
examples.english: Such a cost overrun worries local taxpayers.

blocks.tip: "Une candidature" (a bid/application) is feminine even though it can refer to a whole city or country applying to host an event.

blocks.heading: Les retombées : bénéfices et coûts
blocks.body: Supporters point to les retombées économiques: tourism, jobs, and le rayonnement international a host city gains. Critics counter with the image of un éléphant blanc — a costly stadium built for the event that stands empty afterward, its reconversion (repurposing) proving harder than planners promised. Both claims are debated, and the real balance sheet often only becomes clear years later.

examples.french: Les retombées économiques restent difficiles à mesurer précisément.
examples.english: The economic spin-offs remain hard to measure precisely.

examples.french: Le tourisme a bondi pendant les deux semaines de compétition.
examples.english: Tourism surged during the two weeks of competition.

examples.french: Certains stades sont devenus de véritables éléphants blancs.
examples.english: Some stadiums have become real white elephants.

examples.french: La reconversion du village des athlètes a pris plusieurs années.
examples.english: Repurposing the athletes' village took several years.

examples.french: L'événement a offert un rayonnement international inédit à la ville.
examples.english: The event gave the city unprecedented international exposure.

blocks.tip: "Un éléphant blanc" is a vivid idiom for any costly project that becomes useless — memorable for B2 debate vocabulary.

blocks.heading: Le débat public
blocks.body: Big events rarely go unchallenged: un opposant may organise une manifestation or a pétition against public spending, while un partisan defends l'investissement public as good for the whole region. La polémique often centres on who really benefits — and a partenariat public-privé is sometimes proposed as a compromise, sharing both risk and reward between the state and private companies.

examples.french: Une pétition contre le projet a recueilli des milliers de signatures.
examples.english: A petition against the project gathered thousands of signatures.

examples.french: Les opposants dénoncent le coût pour les contribuables.
examples.english: Opponents denounce the cost to taxpayers.

examples.english: The controversy grows as the date approaches.

examples.french: Les partisans du projet insistent sur l'héritage laissé à la ville.
examples.english: Supporters of the project stress the legacy left to the city.

blocks.heading: Les connecteurs de contraste
blocks.body: Weighing costs against benefits requires precise contrast connectors. Cependant and toutefois (however) soften a shift; en revanche and par contre (on the other hand) mark a sharper opposition; alors que and tandis que (whereas) contrast two facts within a single sentence. Choosing the right one signals exactly how strongly you're pushing back against the previous point.

examples.french: L'événement a boosté le tourisme ; il a cependant coûté très cher.
examples.english: The event boosted tourism; it was, however, very costly.

examples.french: Les partisans vantent l'héritage, en revanche les opposants dénoncent la dette.
examples.english: Supporters praise the legacy; opponents, on the other hand, denounce the debt.

examples.french: Le stade attire les touristes, alors que le village des athlètes reste vide.
examples.english: The stadium attracts tourists, whereas the athletes' village remains empty.

examples.french: Le budget prévoyait dix millions ; il en a coûté trente, toutefois.
examples.english: The budget forecast ten million; it cost thirty, however.

examples.french: La ville a gagné en rayonnement ; par contre, les habitants paient encore la dette.
examples.english: The city gained in international profile; residents, however, are still paying off the debt.

blocks.tip: "En revanche" cannot open a sentence about something negative following something positive alone — it always needs a first clause to contrast against.

blocks.heading: La mise en relief : c'est... qui / c'est... que
blocks.body: To emphasise exactly which element you're debating, French speakers isolate it with c'est... qui (for the subject) or c'est... que (for everything else). This structure is common in spoken argumentation because it lets you land the stress precisely where you want it, rather than relying on intonation alone.

examples.english: It's the taxpayer who ultimately pays the bill.

examples.english: It's the cost overrun that every newspaper is talking about.

blocks.tip: With a plural subject, the verb "être" agrees: "ce sont les bénévoles qui..." not "c'est les bénévoles."

passages.title: Aurenne, dix ans après les Jeux
passages.french:
Dix ans après avoir accueilli les Jeux d'Aurenne, la ville reste divisée sur le bilan de l'événement.
Le comité d'organisation avait promis un héritage durable : de nouveaux transports, des logements, et un rayonnement international pour la région.
Certaines promesses ont été tenues : le tramway construit pour l'occasion dessert aujourd'hui l'ensemble de l'agglomération.
Le village des athlètes, quant à lui, a été reconverti avec succès en quartier résidentiel, une réussite que la mairie met volontiers en avant.
Mais tout n'est pas aussi positif : le grand stade olympique, lui, reste largement sous-utilisé.
On parle aujourd'hui d'un éléphant blanc que la ville peine à entretenir, faute d'événements assez grands pour le remplir.
La dette contractée pour financer les infrastructures pèse encore sur le budget municipal, selon plusieurs élus locaux.
C'est cette dette que critiquent le plus les opposants au projet, qui rappellent que le budget prévisionnel avait été largement dépassé.
Les partisans, eux, insistent sur les retombées économiques et sur le tourisme, qui a doublé depuis les Jeux.
Un partenariat public-privé permet aujourd'hui de financer une partie de l'entretien du stade, une solution jugée insuffisante par certains contribuables.
D'autres villes, en revanche, observent Aurenne de près avant de déposer leur propre candidature.
Le débat, loin d'être clos, illustre bien la complexité d'un tel héritage.
passages.english:
Ten years after hosting the Aurenne Games, the city remains divided over the event's legacy.
The organising committee had promised a lasting legacy: new transport, housing, and international profile for the region.
Some promises were kept: the tram built for the occasion now serves the entire metropolitan area.
The athletes' village, meanwhile, was successfully repurposed into a residential neighbourhood, a success the city council happily highlights.
But not everything is so positive: the large Olympic stadium, for its part, remains largely underused.
People now speak of a white elephant that the city struggles to maintain, for lack of events big enough to fill it.
The debt taken on to finance the infrastructure still weighs on the municipal budget, according to several local officials.
It's this debt that opponents of the project criticise the most, pointing out that the forecast budget was significantly exceeded.
Supporters, for their part, emphasise the economic spin-offs and tourism, which has doubled since the Games.
A public-private partnership now helps finance part of the stadium's upkeep, a solution some taxpayers consider insufficient.
Other cities, on the other hand, are watching Aurenne closely before submitting their own bid.
The debate, far from settled, illustrates well the complexity of such a legacy.
